#0.1 Read the Excel file

```{r}

setwd("C:/Guinea-Pig-data_2/Data")
df_raw <- read_excel("gp2_bodyweight_v2.xlsx", na = c("NA", "N/A", "")   # treat these strings as missing (NA)
)

head(df_raw)
str(df_raw)

```

#1. Cleaning and Structuring the Data

```{r}
#Original columns in the data file:
# diet, compartment, id, week, sex, initial_weight, weekly_weight
# We standardise names, create a unique AnimalID, convert types, and create a centred week variable.

df <- df_raw %>%
rename(
Diet          = diet,
Compartment   = compartment,
ID_label      = id,             # e.g. GREEN/RED/BLUE
Week          = week,
Sex           = sex,
InitialWeight = initial_weight,
Weight        = weekly_weight
) %>%

# Unique animal identifier combining several design variables

unite("AnimalID", Diet, Compartment, ID_label, Sex,
remove = FALSE) %>%
mutate(
Diet          = factor(Diet),
Compartment   = factor(Compartment),
Sex           = factor(Sex),
AnimalID      = factor(AnimalID),
Week          = as.numeric(Week),
InitialWeight = as.numeric(InitialWeight),
Weight        = as.numeric(Weight)
) %>%

# Centre Week for nicer interpretation in the mixed model to to improve model interpretation & stability

mutate(
Week_c = Week - mean(Week, na.rm = TRUE)
)

summary(df)
dplyr::count(df, Diet)
dplyr::count(df, Week)
dplyr::count(df, Sex)
length(unique(df$AnimalID))

```

#2. Derived Growth Metrics per Animal (Final Weight, ADG, RGR)

```{r}
#Here we summarise per animal: Initial weight, Final weight, Duration of trial (in days), Average Daily Gain (ADG), Relative Growth Rate (RGR)
animal_growth <- df %>%
arrange(AnimalID, Week) %>%
group_by(AnimalID, Diet, Sex) %>%
summarise(
InitialWeight = first(InitialWeight),
FinalWeight   = last(Weight),
StartWeek     = first(Week),
EndWeek       = last(Week),
Duration_days = (EndWeek - StartWeek) * 7,
.groups = "drop"
) %>%
mutate(
ADG = (FinalWeight - InitialWeight) / Duration_days,
RGR = (log(FinalWeight) - log(InitialWeight)) / Duration_days
)

summary(animal_growth)

```

#4. Mixed Model for Longitudinal Weight

```{r}
# Ensure df is a plain data.frame
df <- as.data.frame(df)

# Check required columns
needed <- c("Weight","Diet","Week_c","Sex","InitialWeight","AnimalID")
missing <- setdiff(needed, names(df))
if(length(missing) > 0){
  stop("Missing columns: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
}

# Enforce correct types (critical for lmer)
df <- df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    AnimalID      = factor(AnimalID),
    Diet          = factor(Diet),
    Sex           = factor(Sex),
    Week_c        = as.numeric(Week_c),
    Weight        = as.numeric(Weight),
    InitialWeight = as.numeric(InitialWeight)
  ) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na(Weight, Diet, Week_c, Sex, InitialWeight, AnimalID)



install.packages("Matrix")
install.packages("lme4")
library(Matrix)
library(lme4)

mod1 <- lmer(
Weight ~ Diet * Week_c + Sex + InitialWeight +
(1 | AnimalID),
data = df
)

summary(mod1)
anova(mod1)

```

##4.1 Optional: Random slopes for Week within Animal

```{r}
# Base mixed model
mod1 <- lmer(
  Weight ~ Diet * Week_c + Sex + InitialWeight +
    (1 | AnimalID),
  data = df
)

mod1_rs <- lmer(
Weight ~ Diet * Week_c + Sex + InitialWeight +
(Week_c | AnimalID),
data = df
)

anova(mod1, mod1_rs)  # compare intercept-only vs intercept+slope
summary(mod1_rs)

model_use <- mod1_rs

```

#5. Mixed Model Diagnostics and Assumptions
##5.1 Extract fitted values and residuals

```{r}
model_use <- mod1_rs

df_model <- df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(Weight),
    !is.na(InitialWeight),
    !is.na(Week_c)
  )

mod1_rs <- lmer(
  Weight ~ Diet * Week_c + Sex + InitialWeight +
    (Week_c | AnimalID),
  data = df_model
)

df_diag <- df_model %>%
  mutate(
    fitted = fitted(mod1_rs),
    resid  = resid(mod1_rs)
  )

summary(df_diag$resid)

```

##5.2 Residuals vs fitted (linearity & constant variance)

```{r}
ggplot(df_diag, aes(x = fitted, y = resid, colour = Diet)) +
geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
labs(
title = "Mixed model: residuals vs fitted values",
x = "Fitted values",
y = "Residuals"
)

```

##5.3 Residuals vs week (time-related patterns)

```{r}
ggplot(df_diag, aes(x = Week, y = resid, colour = Diet)) +
geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
labs(
title = "Mixed model: residuals vs week",
x = "Week",
y = "Residuals"
)

```

##5.4 Q–Q plot of residuals (normality)

```{r}
qqnorm(df_diag$resid, main = "Mixed model residuals: Q–Q plot")
qqline(df_diag$resid) # not normal

#hence, improve the model

library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(splines)   # for ns()

# 1.1 Ensure key variables are correctly typed
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    Diet          = factor(Diet),
    Sex           = factor(Sex),
    AnimalID      = factor(AnimalID),
    Week          = as.numeric(Week),
    InitialWeight = as.numeric(InitialWeight),
    Weight        = as.numeric(Weight)
  )

# 1.2 Centre Week (helps interpretation & stability)
df <- df %>%
  mutate(Week_c = Week - mean(Week, na.rm = TRUE))

# 1.3 Create modelling dataset with COMPLETE cases
df_model <- df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(Weight),
    !is.na(InitialWeight),
    !is.na(Week_c)
  )

nrow(df_model)     # should be 743 in your case
length(unique(df_model$AnimalID))  # check still 80 animals


#Fit three candidate mixed models
# 2.1 Linear time effect (your current structure)
mod_lin <- lmer(
  Weight ~ Diet * Week_c + Sex + InitialWeight +
    (Week_c | AnimalID),
  data = df_model
)

# 2.2 Quadratic time effect (captures curvature)
mod_quad <- lmer(
  Weight ~ Diet * poly(Week_c, 2, raw = TRUE) + Sex + InitialWeight +
    (Week_c | AnimalID),
  data = df_model
)

# 2.3 Spline time effect (flexible nonlinearity)
mod_spline <- lmer(
  Weight ~ Diet * ns(Week_c, df = 3) + Sex + InitialWeight +
    (Week_c | AnimalID),
  data = df_model
)

#Compare model fits
AIC(mod_lin, mod_quad, mod_spline)


# choose the best model programmatically:
aic_tab <- AIC(mod_lin, mod_quad, mod_spline)
aic_tab

best_name <- rownames(aic_tab)[ which.min(aic_tab$AIC) ]
best_name

# pick the best model object
model_best <- switch(
  best_name,
  "mod_lin"    = mod_lin,
  "mod_quad"   = mod_quad,
  "mod_spline" = mod_spline
)

summary(model_best)


#Diagnostics for the improved model
##Create diagnostic data frame
df_diag <- df_model %>%
  mutate(
    fitted = fitted(model_best),
    resid  = resid(model_best)
  )


##Residuals vs fitted values
ggplot(df_diag, aes(x = fitted, y = resid, colour = Diet)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  labs(
    title = "Improved mixed model: residuals vs fitted values",
    x = "Fitted values (predicted weight)",
    y = "Residuals"
  )

## Q-Q PLOT
ggplot(df_diag, aes(sample = resid)) +
  stat_qq() +
  stat_qq_line() +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  labs(
    title = "Improved mixed model: Q–Q plot of residuals",
    x = "Theoretical quantiles",
    y = "Sample quantiles"
  ) # still not good


```

#6. Model-Based Growth Curves (Adjusted for Initial Weight)

```{r}
newdat <- expand.grid(
Diet   = levels(df$Diet),
Sex    = levels(df$Sex),
Week_c = seq(min(df$Week_c), max(df$Week_c), length.out = 100)
)

newdat$Week <- newdat$Week_c + mean(df$Week, na.rm = TRUE)

mean_init <- mean(df$InitialWeight, na.rm = TRUE)
newdat$InitialWeight <- mean_init

newdat$fit <- predict(model_use, newdata = newdat, re.form = NA)

ggplot() +
geom_point(data = growth_summary,
aes(x = Week, y = mean, colour = Diet),
alpha = 0.5) +
geom_line(data = newdat,
aes(x = Week, y = fit, colour = Diet),
size = 1.1) +
facet_wrap(~ Sex) +
theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
labs(
title = "Model-predicted growth curves (adjusted for initial weight)",
x = "Week",
y = "Body weight"
)

## next option
# Extract fixed effects
fixef(model_use)

# Compute slopes for each Diet group
slope_T1 <- fixef(model_use)["Week_c"]
slope_T2 <- fixef(model_use)["Week_c"] + fixef(model_use)["DietT2:Week_c"]
slope_T3 <- fixef(model_use)["Week_c"] + fixef(model_use)["DietT3:Week_c"]
slope_T4 <- fixef(model_use)["Week_c"] + fixef(model_use)["DietT4:Week_c"]

slopes <- data.frame(
  Diet  = c("T1", "T2", "T3", "T4"),
  Slope = c(slope_T1, slope_T2, slope_T3, slope_T4)
)

slopes

## next option

library(emmeans)

emm_slopes <- emtrends(model_use, specs = "Diet", var = "Week_c")
emm_slopes
confint(emm_slopes)
pairs(emm_slopes)   # pairwise growth-rate comparisons


# Prepare annotation table
annot_df <- data.frame(
  Diet  = c("T1","T2","T3","T4"),
  Sex   = rep(levels(df$Sex), each = 4),
  Week  = min(df$Week) + 0.5,
  BodyWeight = min(df$Weight) + 20,
  Label = paste0("Slope = ", round(slopes$Slope, 2), " g/wk")
)


#add numeric slopes #################

library(tidyverse)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Compute diet-specific weekly growth slopes from model
# ---------------------------------------------------------
fix <- fixef(model_use)

slopes <- tibble(
  Diet  = c("T1", "T2", "T3", "T4"),
  Slope = c(
    fix["Week_c"],
    fix["Week_c"] + fix["DietT2:Week_c"],
    fix["Week_c"] + fix["DietT3:Week_c"],
    fix["Week_c"] + fix["DietT4:Week_c"]
  )
)

# Colourblind-friendly palette
cb_palette <- c(
  "T1" = "#E69F00",
  "T2" = "#009E73",
  "T3" = "#0072B2",
  "T4" = "#CC79A7"
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Build annotation block (slopes)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
label_block <- slopes %>%
  mutate(Label = paste0(Diet, ": ", round(Slope, 1), " g/week")) %>%
  summarise(
    Label_block = paste(Label, collapse = "\n"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Compute ranges per sex for label and legend placement
# ---------------------------------------------------------
range_df <- newdat %>%
  group_by(Sex) %>%
  summarise(
    x_min = min(Week), x_max = max(Week),
    y_min = min(fit),  y_max = max(fit),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # annotation block location (bottom-right)
    x_annot = x_max - 0.5,
    y_annot = y_min + 0.10 * (y_max - y_min),

    # legend title position
    x_legend = x_max - 0.5,
    y_legend = y_min + 0.30 * (y_max - y_min),

    # per-item vertical spacing
    dy = 0.05 * (y_max - y_min)
  )

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Construct internal legend rows for each facet
# ---------------------------------------------------------
legend_df <- slopes %>%
  crossing(range_df) %>%   # replicate per Sex facet
  mutate(
    y = y_legend - (row_number() * dy),   # stacked legend lines
    x = x_legend,
    Label = Diet
  )

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Combine annotation block with facet coordinates
# ---------------------------------------------------------
facet_labels <- range_df %>%
  crossing(label_block) %>%
  select(Sex, x = x_annot, y = y_annot, Label_block)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Publication-quality plot
# ---------------------------------------------------------
ggplot() +

  # Observed means
  geom_point(
    data = growth_summary,
    aes(x = Week, y = mean, colour = Diet),
    alpha = 0.25, size = 1.4
  ) +

  # Model predictions
  geom_line(
    data = newdat,
    aes(x = Week, y = fit, colour = Diet),
    size = 1.2
  ) +

  # Internal legend (points + labels)
  geom_point(
    data = legend_df,
    aes(x = x, y = y, colour = Diet),
    size = 3
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = legend_df,
    aes(x = x + 0.2, y = y, label = Label, colour = Diet),
    hjust = 0, size = 4, fontface = "bold"
  ) +

  # Annotation block (slopes)
  geom_label(
    data = facet_labels,
    aes(x = x, y = y, label = Label_block),
    hjust = 1, vjust = 0,
    size = 4, fontface = "bold",
    fill = "white", alpha = 0.85,
    linewidth = 0.3,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +

  facet_wrap(~ Sex) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cb_palette) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.10))) +

  theme_bw(base_size = 15) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 13, hjust = 0.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Model-Predicted Growth Curves (Adjusted for Initial Weight)",
    subtitle = "Internal legend + internal slope annotation",
    x        = "Week",
    y        = "Body weight (g)"
  )

## =========================================================
## Guinea pig bodyweight analysis: clean + high-impact outputs
## Baseline: InitialWeight ~ Diet * Sex (ART if needed)
## Growth: Weight ~ Diet * Week_c + Sex + InitialWeight + (Week_c | AnimalID)
## Figures: (1) baseline distribution + means, (2) model-based growth curves + CI
## =========================================================

## 1) Packages (install once if needed)
# install.packages(c("tidyverse","readxl","lme4","lmerTest","emmeans","effectsize","performance","ARTool"))
install.packages("janitor")
library(janitor)
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(emmeans)
library(effectsize)
library(performance)
library(ARTool)

## 2) Read + clean (minimal, using your stated column names)
setwd("C:/Guinea-Pig-data_2/Data")

dat <- read_excel("gp2_bodyweight_v2.xlsx", na = c("NA","N/A","")) %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%   # diet, id, week, sex, initial_weight, weekly_weight
  
  transmute(
    Diet          = factor(diet),
    ID            = factor(id),
    week          = as.numeric(week),
    Sex           = factor(sex),
    InitialWeight = as.numeric(initial_weight),
    Weight        = as.numeric(weekly_weight),
    AnimalID      = factor(paste(Diet, ID, Sex, sep = "_"))
  ) %>%
  drop_na(Diet, ID, Week, Sex, InitialWeight, Weight, AnimalID) %>%
  mutate(
    Week_c = Week - mean(Week, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# quick sanity
count(dat, Diet)
count(dat, Sex)
length(unique(dat$AnimalID))

## =========================================================
## 3) BASELINE CHECK (InitialWeight)
## =========================================================

#initial weight data in this dataset are repeated to match weekly observations,
#incomplete relative to the original allocation dataset,
#used here as a covariate, not as a randomisation check.
#Therefore, testing baseline balance using this reshaped dataset is statistically inappropriate.



## =========================================================
## 4) LONGITUDINAL GROWTH MODEL (mixed model)
## =========================================================

# One strong model (random intercept + random slope for week within animal)
mod_g <- lmer(
  Weight ~ Diet * Week_c + Sex + InitialWeight + (Week_c | AnimalID),
  data = dat,
  REML = FALSE
)

# Report-ready table: fixed effects + Type III ANOVA
cat("\nGrowth model: fixed effects summary\n")
print(summary(mod_g))

cat("\nGrowth model: Type III tests (Diet, Week, Diet×Week etc.)\n")
print(anova(mod_g, type = 3))

# Optional: model quality checks (quick)
# performance::check_model(mod_g)  # interactive plots

# High-impact inference for growth: diet-specific slopes (g/week) and their comparisons
emm_slopes <- emtrends(mod_g, specs = "Diet", var = "Week_c")
emm_slopes_ci <- confint(emm_slopes)
pairs_slopes  <- pairs(emm_slopes, adjust = "tukey")

cat("\nDiet-specific growth slopes (g/week):\n")
print(emm_slopes_ci)

cat("\nPairwise comparisons of slopes (Tukey-adjusted):\n")
print(pairs_slopes)


## =========================================================
## 5) JOURNAL-READY GROWTH FIGURE (model-based curves + 95% CI)
## =========================================================

library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(emmeans)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

## --- 0) Fit model (stable)
mod_g <- lmer(
  Weight ~ Diet * Week_c + Sex + InitialWeight + (1 + Week_c || AnimalID),
  data = dat,
  REML = FALSE,
  control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))
)

## --- 1) Sequence of week values on centered scale
week_seq <- seq(min(dat$Week_c, na.rm = TRUE),
                max(dat$Week_c, na.rm = TRUE),
                length.out = 120)

week_mean <- mean(dat$Week, na.rm = TRUE)
init_mean <- mean(dat$InitialWeight, na.rm = TRUE)

## --- 2) Colour-blind friendly palette (Okabe–Ito)
okabe_ito <- c("#0072B2","#009E73","#D55E00","#CC79A7","#56B4E9","#E69F00")
diet_cols <- setNames(okabe_ito[seq_along(levels(dat$Diet))], levels(dat$Diet))

## --- 3) Model-based curves with 95% CI using emmip() (robust)
p_growth <- emmip(
  mod_g,
  Diet ~ Week_c | Sex,
  at = list(Week_c = week_seq, InitialWeight = init_mean),
  CIs = TRUE,
  cov.reduce = FALSE
) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = diet_cols) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = diet_cols) +
  labs(x = "Week", y = "Body weight (g)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text  = element_text(colour = "black")
  ) +
  ## relabel x-axis from centered Week_c back to Week
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = pretty(week_seq, n = 6),
    labels = function(x) round(x + week_mean, 0)
  )

p_growth



###################adjusted, sex-specific baseline (differences at initial weight adjusted)

library(emmeans)
library(ggplot2)

# --- model already fitted as mod_g ---
# mod_g <- lmer(Weight ~ Diet*Week_c + Sex + InitialWeight + (1 + Week_c || AnimalID), data=dat, ...)

week_seq  <- seq(min(dat$Week_c, na.rm=TRUE), max(dat$Week_c, na.rm=TRUE), length.out = 120)
week_mean <- mean(dat$Week, na.rm=TRUE)
init_mean <- mean(dat$InitialWeight, na.rm=TRUE)

# Okabe–Ito palette (colour-blind friendly)
```

##7.4 Diagnostics: ggplot residuals vs fitted

```{r}
# 1. Create a clean dataset actually used in final_mod
final_data <- animal_growth %>%
  drop_na(FinalWeight, InitialWeight)   # keeps only rows used in lm()

# Check that lengths match
nrow(final_data)        # should be 71
length(fitted(final_mod))  # should also be 71

# 2. Build diagnostic data frame
final_diag <- final_data %>%
  mutate(
    fitted = fitted(final_mod),
    resid  = resid(final_mod)
  )

# 3. Residuals vs fitted plot
ggplot(final_diag, aes(x = fitted, y = resid, colour = Diet)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  labs(
    title = "Final weight ANCOVA: residuals vs fitted",
    x     = "Fitted final weight (g)",
    y     = "Residuals (g)"
  )

# 4. Q–Q plot for ANCOVA residuals
qq_df <- data.frame(resid = resid(final_mod))

ggplot(qq_df, aes(sample = resid)) +
  stat_qq() +
  stat_qq_line() +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  labs(
    title = "Final weight ANCOVA: Q–Q plot of residuals",
    x     = "Theoretical quantiles",

## maina code

############################################################
## FINAL WEIGHT ANALYSIS + JOURNAL-READY PLOT
############################################################

## 0. Packages -------------------------------------------------
## Install ONCE if needed:
# install.packages(c("tidyverse", "readxl", "emmeans", "multcompView"))

library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(emmeans)
library(multcompView)

## 1. Read and prepare the longitudinal data -------------------
## Edit the filename/path as needed

# Example: Excel
# df_raw <- read_excel("guineapig_weights.xlsx")

# OR: CSV
# df_raw <- read.csv("guineapig_weights.csv")

# Here I assume your object is called df_raw
df <- df_raw %>%
  rename(
    Diet          = diet,
    ID            = id,
    Week          = week,
    Sex           = sex,
    InitialWeight = initial_weight,
    Weight        = weekly_weight
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Diet          = factor(Diet),
    ID            = factor(ID),
    Sex           = factor(Sex),
    Week          = as.numeric(Week),
    InitialWeight = as.numeric(InitialWeight),
    Weight        = as.numeric(Weight)
  )

## 2. Build ANIMAL-LEVEL dataset: Initial & Final weight -------
## For each animal: first InitialWeight, last non-NA Weight

animal_growth <- df %>%
  arrange(ID, Week) %>%
  group_by(ID, Diet, Sex) %>%
  summarise(
    InitialWeight = first(InitialWeight),
    FinalWeight   = last(Weight[!is.na(Weight)]),
    .groups       = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # keep only complete cases
  filter(!is.na(InitialWeight), !is.na(FinalWeight))

# Quick check
summary(animal_growth)
count(animal_growth, Diet, Sex)

## 3. ANCOVA model: FinalWeight ~ Diet + Sex + InitialWeight ----

final_mod <- lm(
  FinalWeight ~ Diet + Sex + InitialWeight,
  data = animal_growth
)

summary(final_mod)   # coefficients
anova(final_mod)     # F-tests for Diet, Sex, InitialWeight

## 4. Estimated marginal means for Diet (adjusted for InitialWeight) ----

emm_final <- emmeans(
  final_mod,
  ~ Diet,
  cov.reduce = list(InitialWeight = mean)   # adjust at mean initial weight
)

emm_final                     # adjusted means table
pairs(emm_final, adjust = "tukey")  # pairwise diet comparisons

## 5. Build data frame for plotting + significance letters ------

# Turn emmeans results into data frame with CIs
emm_df <- as.data.frame(emm_final)   # has emmean, SE, lower.CL, upper.CL

# Pairwise Tukey comparisons as data frame
pair_df <- as.data.frame(pairs(emm_final, adjust = "tukey"))

# Construct named vector of p-values "T1-T2", "T1-T3", ...
p_vec <- pair_df$p.value
names(p_vec) <- pair_df$contrast

# Convert p-values into compact letter display (a, b, ab, ...)
letters <- multcompLetters(p_vec)$Letters

letters_df <- data.frame(
  Diet    = names(letters),
  Letters = letters,
  row.names = NULL
)

# Merge letters into emm_df
emm_plot_df <- emm_df %>%
  left_join(letters_df, by = "Diet")

emm_plot_df   # this is what we will plot

## 6. Journal-ready plot: adjusted final weight by Diet --------

# Colourblind-friendly palette
cb_palette <- c(
  "T1" = "#E69F00",
  "T2" = "#009E73",
  "T3" = "#0072B2",
  "T4" = "#CC79A7"
)

ggplot(emm_plot_df,
       aes(x = Diet, y = emmean, colour = Diet)) +
  # points = adjusted means
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  # error bars = 95% CI
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL),
    width = 0.12,
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  # significance letters just above CI
  geom_text(
    aes(y = upper.CL + 10, label = Letters),
    colour = "black",
    size = 5,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cb_palette) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position    = "none",
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text          = element_text(colour = "black"),
    plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Adjusted final body weight of guinea pigs by diet",
    x     = "Diet",
    y     = "Final body weight (g, adjusted for initial weight)"
  )

## other plot options

# assumes:
# - animal_growth has Diet, FinalWeight, InitialWeight, Sex
# - emm_plot_df has Diet, emmean, lower.CL, upper.CL, Letters
# - cb_palette is your named colour vector for T1–T4

library(tidyverse)

ggplot() +

  ) +

#Adjusted final weight

library(tidyverse)
library(emmeans)

## 1) Fit ANCOVA with Diet × Sex + InitialWeight
final_mod_sex <- lm(
  FinalWeight ~ Diet * Sex + InitialWeight,
  data = animal_growth
)

## 2) Type III-like ANOVA table (use car::Anova if you prefer Type III)
# Base R anova() is sequential (Type I). For factorial ANCOVA, Type II/III is often preferred.
# If you want Type II/III, uncomment the car line.
# library(car)
# an_tab <- as.data.frame(car::Anova(final_mod_sex, type = 3))

an_tab <- as.data.frame(anova(final_mod_sex)) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("term")

## 3) Helper to safely pull F and p columns (works across table formats)
get_col <- function(df, patterns) {
  nm <- names(df)
  hit <- unique(unlist(lapply(patterns, function(p) grep(p, nm, value = TRUE))))
  if (length(hit) < 1) stop("Could not find expected column in ANOVA table.")
  hit[1]
}

F_col <- get_col(an_tab, c("^F$","F value","F\\.value"))
p_col <- get_col(an_tab, c("Pr\\(>F\\)","^p$","p-value","p\\.value"))

## 4) Build a compact stats label (edit to your preferred terms)
keep_terms <- c("Diet", "Sex", "Diet:Sex", "InitialWeight")

stat_df <- an_tab %>%
  filter(term %in% keep_terms) %>%
  mutate(
    F_val = .data[[F_col]],
    p_val = .data[[p_col]],
    term_lab = recode(term,
                      "Diet" = "Diet",
                      "Sex" = "Sex",
                      "Diet:Sex" = "Diet×Sex",
                      "InitialWeight" = "Initial wt")
  )

fmt_p <- function(p){
  ifelse(is.na(p), "NA",
         ifelse(p < 0.001, "<0.001", formatC(p, digits = 3, format = "f")))
}

stat_text <- paste0(
  stat_df$term_lab,
  ": F=", formatC(stat_df$F_val, digits = 2, format = "f"),
  ", p=", fmt_p(stat_df$p_val),
  collapse = "\n"
)

## 5) EMMs: Diet within Sex at mean InitialWeight
emm_final_sex <- emmeans(
  final_mod_sex,
  ~ Diet | Sex,
  at = list(InitialWeight = mean(animal_growth$InitialWeight, na.rm = TRUE))
)

emm_df <- as.data.frame(summary(emm_final_sex, infer = TRUE)) %>%
  rename(lower = lower.CL, upper = upper.CL) %>%
  mutate(
    Sex  = factor(Sex),
    Diet = factor(Diet)
  )

## 6) Position annotation within each facet (top-left)
ann_df <- emm_df %>%
  group_by(Sex) %>%
  summarise(
    x = 1,  # leftmost diet (works if Diet levels are ordered)
    y = max(upper, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(label = stat_text)

## 7) Journal-ready plot (y-axis from 0) + statistics annotation
p_final_weight <- ggplot(emm_df, aes(x = Diet, y = emmean, colour = Diet)) +

  geom_point(size = 3.2) +

  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.9) +

  facet_wrap(~ Sex, nrow = 1) +

  # stats block (same text in each Sex panel)
  geom_text(
    data = ann_df,
    aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    hjust = 0, vjust = 1,
    size = 3.6,
    colour = "black",
    lineheight = 1.05
  ) +

  scale_colour_manual(values = cb_palette) +

  # start y-axis at zero; keep some headroom for annotation
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, NA)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.10))) +

  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Diet",
    y = "Final body weight (g; adjusted)"
  )

p_final_weight

# export
ggsave(
  filename = "Final_adjusted_body weight.pdf",
  plot     = p_final_weight,
  width    = 180,   # mm (typical journal column width)
  height   = 120,   # mm
  units    = "mm")
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# Load Excel file

# Clean and prepare
adg_plot_df <- adg_raw %>%
  rename(
    Diet     = diet,
    Sex      = sex,
    Week     = week,
    Mean_ADG = Mean_ADG,
    N        = n,
    SEM_ADG  = SEM_ADG
  ) %>%
  mutate(

    Sex      = factor(Sex, levels = c("F", "M")),
    Week     = as.numeric(Week),
    lower    = Mean_ADG - 1.96 * SEM_ADG,
    upper    = Mean_ADG + 1.96 * SEM_ADG,
    lower    = ifelse(lower < 0, 0, lower),  # clamp to zero
    Panel    = recode(Sex, "F" = "Females", "M" = "Males")
  )


######### Plot – ADG vs Week (Overall, no sex), show confidence intervals
# wider CI MEANS HIGHER VARIABILITY, NARROW CI = MORE STABLE GROWTH, LESS VARIABILITY

# Load required packages

library(tidyverse)
library(ggthemes)

# ------------------------------------------------------
# 1️⃣ Summarise Overall ADG (Diet × Week)
# ------------------------------------------------------
adg_overall <- adg_plot_df %>%
  group_by(Diet, Week) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_ADG = mean(Mean_ADG, na.rm = TRUE),
    SEM_ADG  = sqrt(sum(SEM_ADG^2, na.rm = TRUE)) / n(),
    N        = sum(N, na.rm = TRUE),
    lower    = pmax(0, Mean_ADG - 1.96 * SEM_ADG),
    upper    = Mean_ADG + 1.96 * SEM_ADG,
    .groups  = "drop"
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------
# 2️⃣ Define clean publication palette
# ------------------------------------------------------
diet_palette <- c(
  "T1" = "#E69F00",  # orange
  "T2" = "#009E73",  # green
  "T3" = "#0072B2",  # blue
  "T4" = "#CC79A7"   # pink-magenta
)

# ------------------------------------------------------
# 3️⃣ Journal-ready plot with baseline buffer
# ------------------------------------------------------
pB_adg_overall <- ggplot(adg_overall,
                         aes(x = Week, y = Mean_ADG,
                             colour = Diet, fill = Diet, group = Diet)) +

  # Shaded 95% CI ribbon
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
              alpha = 0.25, colour = NA) +

  # Mean line
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +

  # Mean points scaled by sample size (N)
  geom_point(aes(size = N),
             shape = 21, fill = "white", colour = "black", stroke = 0.7) +

  # Manual colors for Diet
  scale_colour_manual(values = diet_palette) +
  scale_fill_manual(values  = diet_palette) +

  # Axis scaling and buffer to prevent overlap with baseline
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 1:10,
    expand = expansion(add = c(0.3, 0.3))   # small horizontal padding
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.08))  # adds ~5% space below x-axis
  ) +

  # Legend for number of weekly replicates
  scale_size_continuous(name = "n (weeks)",
                        range = c(1.5, 4)) +

  # Clean, minimalist journal theme
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position    = "right",
    legend.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    legend.text        = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    axis.title.y       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    axis.text          = element_text(colour = "black", size = 11),
    strip.text         = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle      = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5, colour = "grey30"),
    legend.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "grey80"),
    plot.margin        = margin(t = 10, r = 20, b = 15, l = 15)
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Weekly Average Daily Gain (ADG) of Guinea Pigs by Diet (±95% CI)",
    subtitle = "Mean weekly ADG (g/day) across 10 weeks; shaded areas show 95% confidence intervals",
    x        = "Week",
    y        = "Mean ADG (g/day)"
  )

##############################################################
# MAIN ANALYSIS FOR ADG

############################################################
## GP2 ADG ANALYSIS (Weeks as replicates) — Sections 1 to 4
############################################################

## =========================
## 1) Packages + Import Data
## =========================
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(car)
library(emmeans)
library(ARTool)

# ---- Read + clean
data_adg <- read_excel("GP2_ADG.xlsx", na = c("NA", "N/A", "")) %>%
  rename(
    Diet     = diet,
    Sex      = sex,
    Week     = week,
    Mean_ADG = Mean_ADG,
    SD_ADG   = SD_ADG,
    SEM_ADG  = SEM_ADG,
    N        = n
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Diet     = factor(Diet),
    Sex      = factor(Sex, levels = c("F","M"), labels = c("Females","Males")),
    Week     = as.numeric(Week),
    Mean_ADG = as.numeric(Mean_ADG),
    SD_ADG   = as.numeric(SD_ADG),
    SEM_ADG  = as.numeric(SEM_ADG),
    N        = as.integer(N)
  ) %>%
  drop_na(Diet, Sex, Week, Mean_ADG)

glimpse(data_adg)


## ===============================================
## 2) Assumption checks (2-way model residuals)
## ===============================================
mod_adg_aov <- aov(Mean_ADG ~ Diet * Sex, data = data_adg)

res_adg <- residuals(mod_adg_aov)
shap_p  <- shapiro.test(res_adg)$p.value

lev_p <- car::leveneTest(
  Mean_ADG ~ interaction(Diet, Sex),
  data = data_adg
)[1, "Pr(>F)"]

cat("\nBaseline diagnostics:\n")
cat("  Shapiro p =", signif(shap_p, 4), "\n") # normal 
cat("  Levene  p =", signif(lev_p, 4), "\n")# homogenous


## ==========================================================
## 3) Inference: ANOVA if OK, otherwise ART factorial ANOVA
## ==========================================================
assumptions_ok <- (shap_p > 0.05) && (lev_p > 0.05)

if (assumptions_ok) {
  cat("\nADG inference: 2-way ANOVA (Diet × Sex)\n")
  an_tab <- anova(mod_adg_aov)
  print(an_tab)

  # Diet comparisons within each sex (Tukey)
  emm <- emmeans(mod_adg_aov, ~ Diet | Sex)
  print(emm)
  print(pairs(emm, adjust = "tukey"))

  fit_used <- "ANOVA"

} else {
  cat("\nADG inference: ART factorial ANOVA (robust)\n")
  mod_adg_art <- ARTool::art(Mean_ADG ~ Diet * Sex, data = data_adg)
  an_tab <- anova(mod_adg_art)
  print(an_tab)

  # Post-hoc Diet within Sex using aligned model for Diet:Sex
  art_int <- ARTool::artlm(mod_adg_art, "Diet:Sex")
  emm <- emmeans(art_int, ~ Diet | Sex)
  print(emm)
  print(pairs(emm, adjust = "tukey"))

  fit_used <- "ART"
}


## ==========================================================
## 4) Journal-ready figure + export (Weeks as replicates)
## ==========================================================
diet_palette <- c(
  "T1" = "#E69F00",
  "T2" = "#009E73",
  "T3" = "#0072B2",
  "T4" = "#CC79A7"
)

# Dynamic y padding so boxes/whiskers don't touch the x-axis
y_max <- max(data_adg$Mean_ADG, na.rm = TRUE)
y_pad <- 0.12 * y_max

p_adg <- ggplot(data_adg, aes(x = Diet, y = Mean_ADG, fill = Diet)) +

  geom_boxplot(
    alpha = 0.92,
    width = 0.62,
    outlier.shape  = 21,
    outlier.size   = 2.3,
    outlier.stroke = 0.45,
    outlier.fill   = "white",
    colour         = "black",
    linewidth      = 0.75
  ) +

  # mean dot
  stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "point",
    shape = 21,
    size = 3.1,
    fill = "white",
    colour = "black",
    stroke = 0.9
  ) +

  facet_wrap(~ Sex, nrow = 1) +

  scale_fill_manual(values = diet_palette) +

  # start at 0 + add headroom so geoms don't touch x-axis
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, y_max + y_pad), clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.03, 0.06))) +

  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid      = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6),
```

# 9. ADFI data

```{r}

############################################################
## GP2 — ADFI ANALYSIS + JOURNAL-READY FIGURES (CLEAN SCRIPT)
############################################################

## =========================
## 1) Packages
## =========================
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(writexl)
library(car)
library(ARTool)
library(emmeans)

## =========================
## 2) Import + prepare data
## =========================
feed_raw <- read_excel("GP2_Feedintake.xlsx", na = c("NA", "N/A", "")) %>%
  janitor::clean_names()

# Standardise + create week
feed_df <- feed_raw %>%
  transmute(
    Day  = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(day)),
    Diet = factor(toupper(as.character(diet)), levels = c("T1","T2","T3","T4")),
    Sex  = case_when(
      toupper(as.character(sex)) %in% c("F","FEMALE","FEMALES") ~ "F",
      toupper(as.character(sex)) %in% c("M","MALE","MALES")     ~ "M",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    Sex  = factor(Sex, levels = c("F","M"), labels = c("Females","Males")),
    ADFI = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(adfi))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Week = ceiling(Day / 7)
  ) %>%
  drop_na(Day, Week, Diet, Sex, ADFI) %>%
  arrange(Sex, Diet, Week, Day)

# Optional export of processed daily file (for traceability)
write_xlsx(feed_df, "GP2_Feedintake_with_week.xlsx")

## =========================
## 3) Weekly ADFI summary
## =========================
adfi_summary <- feed_df %>%
  group_by(Diet, Sex, Week) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_ADFI = mean(ADFI, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_ADFI   = sd(ADFI, na.rm = TRUE),
    n         = n(),
    SEM_ADFI  = SD_ADFI / sqrt(n),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Sex, Diet, Week)

write_xlsx(adfi_summary, "GP2_ADFI_SUMMARY_DATA.xlsx")

print(adfi_summary, n = 20)

## =========================
## 4) Statistics (weeks as replicates)
##    Diet × Sex on weekly Mean_ADFI
## =========================
mod_aov <- aov(Mean_ADFI ~ Diet * Sex, data = adfi_summary)
resid_aov <- residuals(mod_aov)

shap_p <- shapiro.test(resid_aov)$p.value
lev_p  <- car::leveneTest(Mean_ADFI ~ interaction(Diet, Sex), data = adfi_summary)[1, "Pr(>F)"]

cat("\nBaseline diagnostics (weekly Mean_ADFI):\n")
cat("  Shapiro p =", signif(shap_p, 4), "\n")  # ALL GOOD
cat("  Levene  p =", signif(lev_p, 4), "\n") # ALL GOOD

assumptions_ok <- (shap_p > 0.05) && (lev_p > 0.05)

if (assumptions_ok) {
  cat("\nInference route: 2-way ANOVA (Diet × Sex)\n")
  tab <- anova(mod_aov)
  print(tab)

  # Diet contrasts within Sex (optional; only interpret if Diet main/interaction matters)
  emm <- emmeans(mod_aov, ~ Diet | Sex)
  print(emm)
  print(pairs(emm, adjust = "tukey"))

} else {
  cat("\nInference route: ART factorial ANOVA (robust)\n")
  mod_art <- ARTool::art(Mean_ADFI ~ Diet * Sex, data = adfi_summary)
  tab <- anova(mod_art)
  print(tab)

  art_int <- ARTool::artlm(mod_art, "Diet:Sex")
  emm <- emmeans(art_int, ~ Diet | Sex)
  print(emm)
  print(pairs(emm, adjust = "tukey"))
}

## =========================
## 5) Plot settings
## =========================
diet_palette <- c(
  "T1" = "#E69F00",
  "T2" = "#009E73",
  "T3" = "#0072B2",
  "T4" = "#CC79A7"
)

## =========================
## 6) Plot A: Weekly ADFI by Diet, faceted by Sex (Mean ± SEM)
## =========================
ymax_sex <- max(adfi_summary$Mean_ADFI + adfi_summary$SEM_ADFI, na.rm = TRUE)
y_pad    <- 0.08 * ymax_sex

p_adfi_sex <- ggplot(adfi_summary,
                     aes(x = Week, y = Mean_ADFI, colour = Diet, group = Diet)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.05) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = pmax(0, Mean_ADFI - SEM_ADFI),
                    ymax = Mean_ADFI + SEM_ADFI),
                width = 0.20, linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ Sex, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = diet_palette) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(adfi_summary$Week)),
                     minor_breaks = NULL,
                     expand = expansion(add = c(0.25, 0.25))) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(15, ymax_sex + y_pad), clip = "off") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(colour = "black")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Week of experiment",
    y = "Average daily feed intake (g/animal/day)",
    colour = "Diet"
  )

print(p_adfi_sex)

ggsave("Figure_ADFI_Weekly_by_Diet_Sex.png", p_adfi_sex, width = 10, height = 5, dpi = 600, bg = "white")
ggsave("Figure_ADFI_Weekly_by_Diet_Sex.pdf", p_adfi_sex, width = 10, height = 5, device = cairo_pdf)


## =========================================================
## Overall ADFI vs Diet (weeks as replicates), faceted by sex
## + add ANOVA stats (Diet effect within each sex)
## =========================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(emmeans)
library(ggplot2)

# adfi_summary must exist with columns:
# Diet, Sex (Females/Males), Week, Mean_ADFI, SD_ADFI, n, SEM_ADFI

# -----------------------------
# 1) Build "overall ADFI vs Diet" dataset (weeks = replicates)
#    This keeps each week as a replicate, but collapses over Week in the plot.
# -----------------------------
adfi_by_diet_sex <- adfi_summary %>%
  filter(!is.na(Mean_ADFI), !is.na(Sex), !is.na(Diet)) %>%
  mutate(
    Diet = factor(Diet),
    Sex  = factor(Sex, levels = c("Females","Males"))
  ) %>%
  group_by(Sex, Diet) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_adfi = mean(Mean_ADFI, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_adfi   = sd(Mean_ADFI, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_week    = sum(!is.na(Mean_ADFI)),
    sem_adfi  = sd_adfi / sqrt(n_week),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ymin = pmax(0, mean_adfi - sem_adfi),
    ymax = mean_adfi + sem_adfi
  )

# -----------------------------
# 2) Diet effect ANOVA *within each sex*
#    (This matches your finding that Diet×Sex is significant.)
# -----------------------------
aov_f <- aov(Mean_ADFI ~ Diet, data = filter(adfi_summary, Sex == "Females"))
aov_m <- aov(Mean_ADFI ~ Diet, data = filter(adfi_summary, Sex == "Males"))

tab_f <- anova(aov_f)
tab_m <- anova(aov_m)

get_Fp <- function(tab){
  # robust extraction for base anova tables
  Fv <- tab$`F value`[1]
  pv <- tab$`Pr(>F)`[1]
  list(F = as.numeric(Fv), p = as.numeric(pv))
}

fp_f <- get_Fp(tab_f)
fp_m <- get_Fp(tab_m)

fmt_p <- function(p){
  if (is.na(p)) return("NA")
  if (p < 0.001) return("<0.001")
  formatC(p, digits = 3, format = "f")
}

stats_df <- tibble(
  Sex = factor(c("Females","Males"), levels = c("Females","Males")),
  label = c(
    paste0("Diet ANOVA: F = ", formatC(fp_f$F, digits = 2, format = "f"),
           ", p = ", fmt_p(fp_f$p)),
    paste0("Diet ANOVA: F = ", formatC(fp_m$F, digits = 2, format = "f"),
           ", p = ", fmt_p(fp_m$p))
  )
)

# placement for the annotation in each facet
y_top <- max(adfi_by_diet_sex$ymax, na.rm = TRUE)
y_pad <- 0.10 * y_top

stats_df <- stats_df %>%
  mutate(
    x = 1,                      # left side of x axis (Diet level 1)
    y = y_top + 0.7 * y_pad
  )

# -----------------------------
# 3) Journal-ready plot
# -----------------------------
diet_palette <- c(
  "T1" = "#E69F00",
  "T2" = "#009E73",
  "T3" = "#0072B2",
  "T4" = "#CC79A7"
)

p_adfi_diet_sex <- ggplot(adfi_by_diet_sex,
                          aes(x = Diet, y = mean_adfi, fill = Diet)) +

  # mean bars (overall across weeks) — clean look
  geom_col(width = 0.68, alpha = 0.92, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.55) +

  # SEM error bars
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
                width = 0.16, linewidth = 0.7) +

  # mean points (over bar) to emphasise estimates
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 3.0, fill = "white",
             colour = "black", stroke = 0.9) +

  # per-facet Diet ANOVA stats
  geom_text(
    data = stats_df,
    aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    hjust = 0,
    size = 3.7
  ) +

  facet_wrap(~ Sex, nrow = 1) +

  scale_fill_manual(values = diet_palette) +

  # start at 0 + ensure bars don't touch x-axis
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, y_top + y_pad), clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.03, 0.06))) +

  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"),
    plot.margin = margin(8, 14, 10, 10)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Diet",
    y = "Average daily feed intake (g/animal/day)"
  )

print(p_adfi_diet_sex)

# -----------------------------
# 4) Save high-resolution
# -----------------------------
ggsave("Figure_ADFI_Overall_by_Diet_Faceted_by_Sex.png",
       plot = p_adfi_diet_sex,
       width = 9.2, height = 4.6, dpi = 600, bg = "white")

ggsave("Figure_ADFI_Overall_by_Diet_Faceted_by_Sex.pdf",
       plot = p_adfi_diet_sex,
       width = 9.2, height = 4.6, device = cairo_pdf)
```

# 10. FCR

```{r}
############################################################
## GP2 — FCR ANALYSIS + JOURNAL-READY FIGURE (NO ERRORS)
## Weeks treated as replicates (as per your ADFI/ADG approach)
############################################################

library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(car)
library(emmeans)
library(ARTool)

## =========================
## 1) Load + clean FCR data
## =========================
setwd("C:/Guinea-Pig-data_2/Data")

fcr_data <- read_excel("GP2_FCR_wk.xlsx", na = c("NA", "N/A", "")) %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%   # safe standardisation
  transmute(
    Diet      = factor(toupper(as.character(diet)), levels = c("T1","T2","T3","T4")),
    Sex       = case_when(
      toupper(as.character(sex)) %in% c("F","FEMALE","FEMALES") ~ "F",
      toupper(as.character(sex)) %in% c("M","MALE","MALES")     ~ "M",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    Sex       = factor(Sex, levels = c("F","M"), labels = c("Females","Males")),
    Week      = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(week)),
    FCR       = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(fcr)),
    Mean_ADFI = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(mean_adfi)),
    Mean_ADG  = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(mean_adg))
  ) %>%
  drop_na(Diet, Sex, Week, FCR)

glimpse(fcr_data)

## =========================
## 2) Stats: Diet × Sex on weekly FCR (weeks = replicates)
## =========================
mod_aov <- aov(FCR ~ Diet * Sex, data = fcr_data)
resid_aov <- residuals(mod_aov)

shap_p <- shapiro.test(resid_aov)$p.value
lev_p  <- car::leveneTest(FCR ~ interaction(Diet, Sex), data = fcr_data)[1, "Pr(>F)"]

cat("\nFCR diagnostics:\n")
cat("  Shapiro p =", signif(shap_p, 4), "\n")
cat("  Levene  p =", signif(lev_p, 4), "\n")

assumptions_ok <- (shap_p > 0.05) && (lev_p > 0.05)

fmt_p <- function(p){
  if (is.na(p)) return("NA")
  if (p < 0.001) "<0.001" else formatC(p, digits = 3, format = "f")
}

if (assumptions_ok) {
  cat("\nInference route: 2-way ANOVA (Diet × Sex)\n")
  aov_tab <- anova(mod_aov)
  print(aov_tab)

  F_diet <- aov_tab["Diet", "F value"]; p_diet <- aov_tab["Diet", "Pr(>F)"]
  F_sex  <- aov_tab["Sex",  "F value"]; p_sex  <- aov_tab["Sex",  "Pr(>F)"]
  F_int  <- aov_tab["Diet:Sex","F value"]; p_int <- aov_tab["Diet:Sex","Pr(>F)"]

  stats_text <- paste0(
    "ANOVA (weeks as replicates)\n",
    "Diet: F=", formatC(F_diet, digits = 2, format = "f"), ", p=", fmt_p(p_diet), "\n",
    "Sex: F=",  formatC(F_sex,  digits = 2, format = "f"), ", p=", fmt_p(p_sex),  "\n",
    "Diet×Sex: F=", formatC(F_int, digits = 2, format = "f"), ", p=", fmt_p(p_int)
  )

  fit_used <- "ANOVA"

} else {
  cat("\nInference route: ART factorial ANOVA (robust)\n")
  mod_art <- ARTool::art(FCR ~ Diet * Sex, data = fcr_data)
  art_tab <- as.data.frame(anova(mod_art)) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("Effect")
  print(art_tab)

  # pull F + p safely (ARTool anova has columns: Df, Df.res, F value, Pr(>F))
  F_diet <- art_tab %>% filter(Effect == "Diet")     %>% pull(`F value`)
  p_diet <- art_tab %>% filter(Effect == "Diet")     %>% pull(`Pr(>F)`)
  F_sex  <- art_tab %>% filter(Effect == "Sex")      %>% pull(`F value`)
  p_sex  <- art_tab %>% filter(Effect == "Sex")      %>% pull(`Pr(>F)`)
  F_int  <- art_tab %>% filter(Effect == "Diet:Sex") %>% pull(`F value`)
  p_int  <- art_tab %>% filter(Effect == "Diet:Sex") %>% pull(`Pr(>F)`)

  stats_text <- paste0(
    "ART ANOVA (weeks as replicates)\n",
    "Diet: F=", formatC(F_diet, digits = 2, format = "f"), ", p=", fmt_p(p_diet), "\n",
    "Sex: F=",  formatC(F_sex,  digits = 2, format = "f"), ", p=", fmt_p(p_sex),  "\n",
    "Diet×Sex: F=", formatC(F_int, digits = 2, format = "f"), ", p=", fmt_p(p_int)
  )

  fit_used <- "ART"
}

## Optional: post-hoc Diet within Sex (only if Diet×Sex OR Diet is meaningful)
if (assumptions_ok) {
  emm <- emmeans(mod_aov, ~ Diet | Sex)
  print(emm)
  print(pairs(emm, adjust = "tukey"))
} else {
  art_int <- ARTool::artlm(mod_art, "Diet:Sex")
  emm <- emmeans(art_int, ~ Diet | Sex)
  print(emm)
  print(pairs(emm, adjust = "tukey"))
}

## =========================
## 3) Summary for plotting (means ± SEM across weeks)
## =========================
fcr_overall <- fcr_data %>%
  group_by(Diet, Sex) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_FCR = mean(FCR, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_FCR   = sd(FCR, na.rm = TRUE),
    N_weeks  = n(),
    SEM_FCR  = SD_FCR / sqrt(N_weeks),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ymin = pmax(0, Mean_FCR - SEM_FCR),
    ymax = Mean_FCR + SEM_FCR
  )

## =========================
## 4) Journal-ready plot (faceted by sex + stats text)
## =========================
fcr_palette <- c(
  "T1" = "#E69F00",
  "T2" = "#009E73",
  "T3" = "#0072B2",
  "T4" = "#CC79A7"
)

y_top <- max(fcr_overall$ymax, na.rm = TRUE)
y_pad <- 0.14 * y_top

p_fcr <- ggplot(fcr_overall, aes(x = Diet, y = Mean_FCR, fill = Diet)) +

  # bars
  geom_col(width = 0.66, alpha = 0.92, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +

  # SEM errorbars
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax), width = 0.16, linewidth = 0.75) +

  # mean points (nice for print)
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 3.0, fill = "white", colour = "black", stroke = 0.9) +

  facet_wrap(~ Sex, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = fcr_palette) +

  # start at 0 + add headroom so bars don't touch x-axis
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, y_top + y_pad), clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.03, 0.06))) +

  # stats annotation (top-left of figure area)
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = -Inf, y = Inf,
    label = stats_text,
    hjust = -0.02, vjust = 1.05,
    size = 3.6
  ) +

  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid      = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6),
    strip.text      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    axis.title.x    = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y    = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text       = element_text(colour = "black"),
    plot.margin     = margin(8, 14, 10, 10)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Diet",
    y = "Feed conversion ratio (FCR)"
  )

print(p_fcr)

## =========================
## 5) Save high-resolution
## =========================
ggsave("Figure_FCR_Overall_by_Diet_Faceted_by_Sex.png",
       plot = p_fcr, width = 9.2, height = 4.6, dpi = 600, bg = "white")

ggsave("Figure_FCR_Overall_by_Diet_Faceted_by_Sex.pdf",
       plot = p_fcr, width = 9.2, height = 4.6, device = cairo_pdf)

cat("\nSaved:\n- Figure_FCR_Overall_by_Diet_Faceted_by_Sex.png\n- Figure_FCR_Overall_by_Diet_Faceted_by_Sex.pdf\n")
cat("Inference route used:", fit_used, "\n")
```
